sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Physical Wholesale Brokerage of Marine Fuel Oil and Distillates

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary French legal order; commercial company law codified in the Code de commerce)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-United States Income and Capital Tax Convention (1967, amended by 2009 Protocol)
France-United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Agreement (1979, amended 2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-56 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), including Article L.561-2-2 which sets the 25% beneficial-ownership disclosure test; Article L.561-15 (TRACFIN suspicious-transaction reporting); Article R.123-126 of the French Commercial Code (beneficial-owner register filed with the RCS); Decree No. 2017-650 of 28 April 2017 (UBO registration procedure); Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II) transposing the 4th AML Directive; Directives (EU) 2015/849, (EU) 2018/843 and (EU) 2018/1673 as transposed; ACPR and AMF AML/CFT guidelines.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (French UBO register closed to the public since CJEU Case C-37/20 judgment of 22 November 2022; inspection limited to competent authorities and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport or national identity document of each UBO and proposed SAS director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or notary public of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if origin state is a 1961 Convention contracting party; otherwise consular legalization by the competent French consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorising the French incorporation counsel or a named resident agent to sign the SAS constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (non-Hague states); certified French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of source of funds for capital contributions (SWIFT-confirmed for wire and SBLC routes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate or private bank holding the funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation of signature in the origin jurisdiction; apostille optional but recommended for high-risk files

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing, registration extract and constitutional documents of any foreign corporate shareholder in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry competent for the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; sworn translation into French by a certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO chain declaration and organizational chart certified by each intermediate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Directors of each intermediate holding entity, with notarial certification available
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; bank and counsel attestation for verification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence: (i) PEP and close-associate screening per ACPR guidance; (ii) negative-match screening against the European Union restrictive measures consolidated list published by the French Treasury (DG Trésor), the UN Security Council consolidated list, and OFAC SDN (advisory, binding indirectly through USD clearing); (iii) adverse-media and source-of-funds verification; (iv) TRACFIN reporting obligations under Article L.561-15 of the Code monétaire et financier for any suspicious transaction arising from the marine-fuel commodity flows.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises — https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (operated by INPI); RCS extracts via infogreffe.fr; trademark and name search via data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS denomination may be in French or in a foreign language provided it is written in Latin script and clearly distinguished from registered marks; all constitutional documents must be in French or accompanied by sworn translations; the denomination must include the suffix 'Société par actions simplifiée' or 'SAS' in accordance with Article L.227-2 of the French Commercial Code.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS does not operate a blocking reservation; the statutory clearance is a due-diligence search on INPI, Infogreffe and EUIPO trademark registers. On formal rejection by the Guichet unique, the applicant may (i) file a rectification request correcting the stated objection, (ii) within 15 days of the reasoned refusal petition the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce under Article L.123-46 of the French Commercial Code, and (iii) concurrently file an administrative complaint with the INPI through the Guichet unique; a fresh application with a new denomination is the fastest commercial route.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Administrative virtual office accepted through a regulated domiciliation agreement under Articles R.123-167 et seq. of the French Commercial Code, but commercial-substance rules for a high-risk marine-fuel wholesale brokerage require physical presence with records, personnel and IT; virtual-only operations are not aligned with regulatory expectations for this sector.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — estimated 70-80% probability of unannounced inspection within the first two years by TRACFIN, DGCCRF or Customs (DGDDI) due to the commodity-brokerage risk profile.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory RCS incorporation filing — principal registration of an SAS with the competent Greffe du Tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff (tarif des greffiers) — approximately EUR 87.38 including related levies (2024)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Formal notice of constitution (Avis de constitution) published in an approved legal-notice journal (JAL) prior to Guichet unique submission
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved publisher of legal announcements (Journal d'annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff cap per Article L.210-2 of the French Commercial Code; typical market rate EUR 70-140

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation corporate-name availability and trademark conflict search (INPI, Infogreffe, EUIPO)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Infogreffe / EUIPO databases and counsel's research fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official search database fee plus fixed counsel charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Optional notarization of the SAS bylaws (statuts) where the subscriber is a foreign corporate entity or where in-kind contributions require executory form
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff reference (tarif des notaires); EUR 350-450 market band

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation into French of constitutional documents, UBO declarations, apostilles and KYC pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator (traducteur agréé près la cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed market tariff for commercial and legal documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register declaration preparation, PEP/sanctions/adverse-media screening and TRACFIN due-diligence file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee benchmark for High_Risk_Special_License commodity entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation agreement for the registered office — first year (virtual office upgrade to physical commercial substance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Qualified domiciliary (domiciliataire agréé registered with the Préfecture)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market contract tariff per Articles R.123-167 et seq. of the French Commercial Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization charges for UBO, Power of Attorney and corporate KYC documents abroad
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French Ministry of Justice (Apostille Bureau) and extraterritorial French consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee per document — approximately EUR 100 per apostille, charged per bundle

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée) and Book II, Title II; Decree No. 2023-372 of 13 May 2023 (Guichet unique formalities)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered via the single online portal formalite.entreprises.gouv.fr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificat d'identification au RCS (executive copy of the Articles of Association filed under the electronic single formalities system; issuance of the Extrait K-bis as proof of legal existence)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for SAS under Article L.227-2; capital is set freely in the Articles. Cash contributions must be fully deposited into a blocked escrow account at a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the block is released only upon completion of RCS registration. In-kind contributions must be fully paid-up on subscription; preference shares and share premiums are permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby irrevocably subscribe for the shares comprising the Company's share capital of EUR ______, constitute the said share capital by payment in cash and/or contribution in kind, and authorise the President to deposit the funds into a blocked escrow account with a French credit institution and to collect the deposit certificate. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at ______, France, as the place of central administration and principal establishment. RESOLVED FURTHER, that ______ is appointed as first President of the Company with authority to represent the Company before third parties and to complete the registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, to publish the mandatory legal notice, and to accept all regulatory mandates. The President is authorised to open the Company's corporate banking accounts and to affix the corporate seal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association and Beneficial Owner Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional for private deed; mandatory if real property is contributed) and Fiduciary/Corporate Counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts in French or bilingual French-English (French prevails) under private signature (sous seing privé) or notarial deed (acte authentique). Include corporate form SAS, company name, corporate object (wholesale brokerage of crude oil and refined petroleum products), registered office, share capital, share classes, appointment of the first President, and duration (max. 99 years). All shareholders must sign; the designated President must sign the declaration of non-conviction (déclaration de non-condamnation) and provide identity documentation. Prepare the Declaration of Beneficial Owner (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) listing each shareholder holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (original + two notarised copies if notarial deed)
Declaration of Beneficial Owner (form FORMULAIRE DBE-1)
Identity documents (national ID or passport) of all shareholders and the President
Declaration of non-conviction of the President
Proof of address of the registered office (lease agreement, ownership deed, or domiciliation agreement)
Power of attorney if signing through an authorised representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are rejected for substantive defects, rectify the legal defects by re-execution of a supplementary deed (acte rectificatif) and re-submit to the Registry; if the notary issued a negative opinion, cure by amending the contested clauses and obtain a new notarial act before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital into a Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (bank) or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital deposit account in the name of the company 'en formation'. Deposit the total subscribed cash capital plus any share premium. The bank will issue the Attestation de blocage (certificate of capital blockage) blocking the funds until the President delivers the certificate of registration from the RCS. Upon presentation of the K-bis extract, the funds are released for the benefit of the company.
required_dossiers: Copy of the draft Articles of Association
Identity of the person authorised to receive the exposure certificate (President or co-founder)
Bank's KYC/AML onboarding documents (proof of corporate purpose, source of funds, proof of identity of beneficial owners)
Draft power of attorney for the holder of the temporary account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening under AML/CFT rules, select another French credit institution or file a signal with the ACPR and request a reasoned refusal; where the issue is insufficiency of documentary evidence, remediate by submitting enhanced beneficial owner and source-of-funds declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of a Legal Notice in a Journal of Legal Announcements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorised in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place a public legal notice containing the draft corporate name, legal form (SAS), share capital amount, registered office address, corporate object statement, duration, and names of the shareholders/President. The publisher will provide the Justificatif de parution (attestation of publication) which must be attached to the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Completed legal notice text as supplied by the appointed JAL
File number or project reference from the formation intermediary (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL flags an inconsistency between the notice and the Articles (e.g., office address or corporate object), obtain a corrected publication reprint; if the notice is rejected, publish a rectification notice and obtain a fresh attestation before filing with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Formation Dossier at the RCS via Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI platform) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto formalite.entreprises.gouv.fr, create the agent account, select 'Société par Actions Simplifiée – Constitution', and complete the online M0 declarative flow. Upload all required documents as PDFs, declare the activity code (NAF 46.61Z – wholesale of solid, liquid and gaseous fuels and related products), pay the filing fee (approximately EUR 385, including CFE tax) by electronic card. After validation, the registry issues the RCS registration number and the K-bis extract.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 form (integrated into the electronic interface)
Signed Articles of Association (uploaded PDF)
Attestation de blocage from the bank
Justificatif de parution from the JAL
Declaration of non-conviction of the President
Powers of attorney (if applicable)
Declaration of Beneficial Owner (DBE)
Proof of registered office (lease/domiciliation contract)
Identity documents of shareholders holding at least 25% of capital or voting rights
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a rejet (rejection notice) or demande de régularisation, submit the missing or corrected documents within 15 days via the Guichet Unique portal; if the rejection is maintained, lodge a judicial appeal before the Président du Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of the final rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of the K-bis Extract and Subsequent Post-Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INSEE / URSSAF / Trade Associations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS announces the registration, download the official Extrait K-bis. Use the SIREN and SIRET numbers to register with URSSAF for social contribution, with the Tax Office for VAT (TVA intra-communautaire number) and corporate income tax, and with the Tribunal de Commerce for commerce formalities. Obtain a professional certification for wholesale petroleum products if required.
required_dossiers: Extrait K-bis (issued by the Registry)
RCS SIREN/SIRET number notification
Details of the bank account of the company
VAT/EC registration application (form MO and annexes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or URSSAF registration is delayed, contact the competent French tax office (SIE) or URSSAF delegation directly using the SIREN number and the K-bis extract to request an expedited dossier review and obtain a nominal tax identification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de l'Énergie et du Climat (DGEC), Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires, in coordination with the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'opérateur pétrolier (petroleum operator registration) under Articles L.652-1 and R.652-1 et seq. of the French Energy Code (Code de l'énergie), together with a licence d'importation/exportation de produits pétroliers if physical entry/exit of goods into/from French customs territory is carried out

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires – Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR) and the regional DREAL under the ICPE regime
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 – Registration (autorisation) limited to the wholesale and brokering activity without storage; if any storage of liquid hydrocarbons exceeding 10 tonnes exists, the site falls under ICPE registration, required to file a Dossier de Référence (DR) for Rubrique 1432 (liquides inflammables) and, where applicable, Rubrique 4610/4612 for fuel oil storage; a full EIA (Étude d'impact) is triggered only for facilities classified under the 'autorisation' regime (thresholds of storage volume > 300 m³ or when located in a sensitive zone).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the ICPE Order of 3 October 2010 (arrêté ministériel du 03/10/2010) fixing thresholds for volatile organic compounds (VOC) emissions at installations (0.02 g/m³ VOC recovery efficiency ≥ 90% for petroleum product loading), wastewater discharge limits (total hydrocarbons < 5 mg/L in treated effluents, pH 6.5–8.5, temp < 30°C), and mandatory leak detection and maintenance protocols for storage tanks under ISO 9001 and F-Gas Regulation 517/2014; hazardous waste (e.g., sludges, contaminated mud) must be disposed of through registered waste carriers with full tracking documentation (BSDD).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification - Commission de Sécurité (SDIS) clearance for any location open to the public; structural inspection (verification de stabilité) of storage building, racking and tank foundations by an approved inspection body; workplace visitation clearance by the Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) covering the use of elevated work equipment, hazardous atmospheres, and emergency response plans (Plan d'Opération Interne / POI, where storage is installed); compliance with the code of work (Code du travail) on fire extinguishers, first aid and evacuation drills.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), France; electronic tax filing portal: impots.gouv.fr (professional space 'Espace professionnel'); company incorporation and TIN (SIREN/SIRET) registration through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; VAT registration is processed by the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – File a single electronic M0 application on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, director consent, and non-resident parent corporate documents legalised or apostilled as applicable). Step 2 – The Guichet Unique transmits the dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, which issues the RCS registration, the 9-digit SIREN, the 14-digit SIRET, and the Kbis extract evidencing legal existence. Step 3 – DGFiP automatically assigns the intra-Community VAT number (format 'FR' + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN) and opens the corporate income tax and VAT file with the SIE. Step 4 – If invoicing must commence before the VAT number is allocated, the SAS should use the accelerated SIE pre-registration procedure or, for non-resident entities without a French fixed establishment carrying out taxable supplies in France, appoint a fiscal representative (Article 289 A CGI) and obtain a direct non-resident French VAT number via form 1071-SD.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SAS is mandatorily subject to corporate income tax (IS) under Article 206-1 CGI; no pass-through option and no US-style check-the-box election exist in French law. Available elections: (i) fiscal integration (groupe fiscal intégré) under Article 223 A CGI where a French parent holds at least 95% of the capital and voting rights of its French subsidiaries; (ii) option for the worldwide or consolidated profit regime (bénéfice mondial ou consolidé, Articles 209 quinquies and 209 octies CGI) subject to express DGFiP authorisation; (iii) hybrid-mismatch rules under ATAD 1 and ATAD 2 (Directives (EU) 2016/1164 and 2017/952, transposed by the 2019 and 2020 French Finance Acts) apply automatically to cross-border arrangements with no elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French VAT, harmonised with EU Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base under Article 293 B CGI: EUR 85,000 of annual turnover for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for supplies of services, beyond which VAT registration is mandatory. For this marine-bunker wholesale activity the franchise is practically unavailable and registration is required from the first taxable transaction, as the counterparties are VAT-registered traders and the volume of energy trading under ISIC 4661 exceeds the threshold ab initio.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing reform (Ordonnance 2021-1190, Law 2022-1726, Decree 2024-1267): from 1 September 2026 all French taxable persons must be able to receive structured e-invoices (Factur-X, UBL or CII) and large companies (grandes entreprises and ETIs) must issue e-invoices through an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); from 1 September 2027 all PMEs and micro-enterprises must issue e-invoices. The PDP/PPF performs automated format validation and transfers e-reporting transaction and payment data to DGFiP. France does not apply real-time fiscal stamping or digital seals for VAT; clearance is deferred, but PPF data enables near-real-time risk reconciliation. In parallel, the SAS must file the recapitulative statement of intra-Community supplies and the EU sales list under Article 289 C CGI for movements of fuel products.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating / exemption with credit applies: (i) exports of goods outside the EU at 0% under Article 262-I CGI providing the goods physically leave the EU territory; (ii) intra-Community supplies to a buyer holding a valid EU VAT number at 0% under Article 262 ter CGI; (iii) for this specific marine-fuel scope, supplies of bunker fuel and distillates for the provisioning (avitaillement) of seagoing vessels engaged in international navigation are exempt with deduction under Article 262-II-2° CGI, mirroring Article 14(1)(c) of Directive 2003/96/EC, provided the operator holds the required accise licence and the product is delivered under the excise suspension system (entrepôt fiscal de stockage); (iv) a zero-rating applied without substantiation is recharacterised as a domestic taxable supply at the 20% standard rate. Resulting input-VAT credits from export activity are refundable through the quarterly refund claim form 3517-SD (Article 242-0 C of Annexe II CGI) on presentation of the underlying export documentation bundle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/DEX) validated in the DELTA customs system and exit-confirmed by the French customs office of departure
Bill of Lading (connaissement) or, for intra-EU movement, CMR or air waybill certifying physical removal from France within 90 days
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103 credit proof evidencing payment and foreign-exchange repatriation from the foreign buyer
For intra-Community supplies only: the buyer's validated EU VAT number and the corresponding recapitulative statement (DEB/EU Sales List) entry
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP verifies the 90-day export-evidence rule, the DEB/SAF-T reconciliation, and actual receipt of proceeds within 180 days; where the bundle is incomplete or fraudulent, the zero-rating is clawed back with standard-rate VAT (20%) reinstated retroactively, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% (Article 1727 CGI) and an accuracy penalty of 40% for bad faith (mauvaise foi) or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law (manœuvres frauduleuses / abus de droit, Article 1729 CGI, LPF L64). The French customs authority may additionally enforce excise and customs penalties for undeclared fuel movements under the Code des douanes, including penalties up to the value of the goods for misrepresentation. Non-repatriation of export proceeds is treated as a customs-exchange offence and may trigger a 25% penalty on the unremitted amount, with DGFiP concurrently denying input-VAT deduction on the corresponding supply and rejecting any related VAT refund claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France; cross-border monetary, financial, and foreign exchange reporting is jointly overseen with the Direction Générale du Trésor under French Monetary and Financial Code Articles L.151-1 to L.165-1 and EU Regulation 1847/2019.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a eurozone member, maintains full convertibility of the euro for both current and capital account operations. No prior foreign-exchange authorization is required for ordinary commercial settlement relating to wholesale distribution of crude oil and refined products. However, French-resident entities must file Banque de France cross-border traffic declarations (OFB) for each payment with a non-resident counterparty or account when the transaction exceeds EUR 100,000. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are legally permitted upon demonstration of distributable reserves and actual corporate substance, subject to domestic withholding tax conventions, the interest barrier limitation, transfer-pricing documentation, and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits where applicable. France applies no discriminatory measures against inward foreign direct investment except for EU screening mechanisms applicable to critical sectors; the wholesale petroleum brokerage sector is not subject to foreign-ownership restrictions but does require statutory licensing and compliance with sectoral regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation in France requiring exporters of goods, including petroleum products, to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or to convert foreign currency receipts into euros within any mandatory timeline. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency in French or EU bank accounts. Nonetheless, the French customs authority (DGDDI) requires export declarations for goods above the Intrastat threshold, and Banque de France OFB reporting applies when any individual cross-border cash transaction with a non-resident exceeds EUR 100,000. For treasury prudence, the entity should establish an internal conversion policy limiting open foreign-currency balances to 72 hours and executing conversions through an approved EU credit institution at central mid-market rates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
BPCE - Banque Populaire et Caisse d'Epargne

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury operations and cross-border commodity settlement. Digital electronic-money institutions and Italian/Spanish EMIs operating into France (e.g. Qonto, Shine, Bunq, Wise Business) generally reject wholesale fuel-distribution businesses because of the elevated AML/CFT risk profile. They cannot issue Standby Letters of Credit, handle documentary trade collections, or provide real-time commercial settlement under SWIFT MT103 at the scale required by ISIC 4661. Their viable use is limited to ancillary payroll, local expenses, and card disbursements where the total monthly turnover remains below the EMI's own low-risk threshold, and only when a full-service Tier-1 commercial bank remains the treasury back-bone.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a high-risk energy commodity brokerage vehicle, French Tier-1 banks mandate in-person onboarding for all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and at least one executive director at a metropolitan French branch. A remote video interview is theoretically permitted under French AML/CFT law but is never approved for entities dealing in wholesale refined products without a pre-existing long-term banking relationship. The bank will require a physical visit, original corporate documents, proof of economic substance, notarized signatures, and a genuine interview regarding the business plan, counter-parties, sanction compliance, and source of funds. Second-country directors with residence outside France should expect additional due diligence and biometric identity verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification for wholesale distribution of marine fuel oil and refined distillates; potential for trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain of commercial contracts, purchase and sale confirmations, bill of lading and warehouse receipts, vessel nomination lists, charter-party agreements, independent quantity/quality inspection certificates (SGS, Inspectorate), Incoterms declarations, and documented transport route covering the full supply chain from refinery to end customer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or director appearing as politically exposed person, having tax residency in a grey-listed or sanctioned jurisdiction, or holding multiple shell-company directorships.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated passports, residence permits, official proof of tax residency (e.g. tax assessment notice), TIN numbers, three-month original bank reference letters from a regulated OECD bank, sworn statement of source of wealth, local professional references, notarized UBO declarations, negative sanctions screening results through EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions lists, and a detailed explanation of the commercial rationale for any non-domestic structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound and outbound payments routed via high-risk correspondent banks, private offshore institutions, or jurisdictions with weak beneficial-ownership registries; alleged risk of sanctions evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commitment to route all transactions solely through SWIFT MT103/MT202 via direct Euro-area bank correspondents; complete corporate diagram with intermediate entities; trade contracts identifying all payment routes; refusal of any crypto-currency settlement; historical statements of the ultimate counterparty showing consistent pattern with physical commodities; and a legal representation letter confirming no sanctions-circumvention link.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly created SAS with minimal share capital and no prior financial statements; perceived as a letterbox company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract proving genuine French registration, articles of association, office lease with actual operating presence, corporate substance binder (employment records, authority matrix, physical premises), audited or accountant-prepared interim financials, 12-month cash-flow projection consistent with the trading mandate, and a board resolution approving the treasury policy and banking mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected indirect tax fraud, VAT carousel, or excise-duty evasion involving mineral oil and refined products.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of valid VAT registration and EU VAT number, DGDDI customs import/export entry documentation, excise duty receipts or excise-bond guarantees, evidence of payment of commercial duties (instance via the Compte Niort or the French mineral oil warehouse system), a tax-lawyer opinion on the commodity flow, and periodic reconciliation of the goods flows with financial flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection into the French SAS will be executed by SWIFT wire from the non-resident parent or shareholder, using EUR-denominated transfer to the designated Tier-1 capital escrow account. The French statutory requirement is notification of Banque de France through the OFB reporting system whenever the individual cross-border flow exceeds EUR 100,000, which will always apply for capital injections of the intended size. The bank will require a certified copy of the board resolution, the shareholders' agreement, a certificate of deposit of funds from the legal representative (attestation du dépositaire), an updated Kbis, and UBO declarations. The SWIFT payment must include a clear economic-purpose descriptor such as 'Subscription of share capital' or 'Shareholder current-account advance' and the French purpose code corresponding to a capital transaction; the receiving bank will record the code for OFB transmission. Incoming funds cannot be commingled with trade settlements until the legal existence and share capital increase have been registered with the commercial registry (RCS).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for physical crude oil and refined product purchases will run primarily through the international clearing rail of SWIFT MT103 direct-bank wires from the French operational account to the seller's account, with each instruction stating the precise underlying invoice reference and trade document identifier. Documentary Standby Letters of Credit (SBLC) and Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP600 and URR725 will be used for secured settlement, with the French bank acting as issuing or confirming bank. The entity may open independent import/export accounts in EUR and USD to allow netting of commodity inflows and outflows. For energy-derivative hedging transactions executed on-exchange or bilaterally, settlements will clear through central counterparties (CCPs) under EMIR or, for OTC physical contracts, through SEPA and SWIFT in accordance with the banque de France payment systems rules. All outbound trade disbursements must be matched with an underlying invoice, transport document, insurance policy, and any required export/import license before the bank's trade-processing team will execute payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX Forward (plain vanilla) with a French or EEA licensed credit institution
FX Swap (swap de devises) for short-term liquidity management between EUR and USD
OTC Currency Options (EUR/USD call and put) executed under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA collateral terms
Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) matching the tenor of commodity-trade working-capital facilities

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing non-convertible or illiquid currencies, permitted only when the underlying trading contract creates genuine exposure and the hedging is executed through an EU-regulated investment firm

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax package (liasse fiscale, form 2065 with 2050-series annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (Service des Impôts des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31-December fiscal year-end: second working day following 1 May. For other fiscal year-ends: second working day following the 4th month after the closing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of assessed tax, increased to 10% after 30 days, up to 40% in bad faith; monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%; automatic tax assessment (imposition d'office) and enforced recovery by the public treasury.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, management report (rapport de gestion), and mandatory statutory auditor's report filed with the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via INPI – Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises; publication recorded in BODACC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of fiscal year-end; filing with the register within 1 month of approval (effectively up to 7 months after closing; court-ordered extension possible in exceptional cases)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing greffe surcharges; injunctive order with daily financial penalty (astreinte); persistent non-filing enables the public prosecutor to request court-ordered dissolution or administrative strike-off (radiation); company president exposed to a fine of up to EUR 9,000 for failure to obtain shareholder approval of accounts within the statutory 6-month window.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS identification data and Beneficial Owner Declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI – Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 November (INPI annual confirmation campaign); any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers crossing the direct or indirect 25% threshold, must be filed within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to EUR 7,500 for the legal representative (EUR 37,500 for the legal person); blocking of all subsequent RCS formalities until regularised; suspension of voting and dividend rights of undeclared shareholders; risk of money-laundering classification for hidden ownership chains.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions, including paid-up capital held at least 75% by individuals or qualifying companies. The standard 25% rate applies above that amount. Certain qualifying new enterprises and activities may benefit from narrowly defined exemptions or reliefs; eligibility is fact-specific. The 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax may apply where the statutory turnover and tax-liability thresholds are met.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period. Annual use is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The portion not usable under the cap carries forward. Carryback is generally available to the preceding financial year, subject to a EUR 1 million limit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD and its schedules, filed electronically through the professional tax portal using EDI-TDFC or the applicable DGFiP online service. The detailed tax computation is generally reported on forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD under the normal regime; eligible smaller entities may use the simplified schedule set.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; four corporate income tax instalments during the financial year where required, followed by a balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File the annual return within three months after the financial year-end. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second business day following 1 May, subject to the annual DGFiP calendar and any formally announced extension. Corporate tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December; the balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, SIREN, registered office, principal activity, tax office, financial-year dates, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned French SAS reports its French company details and French tax identifiers. Foreign ownership does not convert the SAS into a non-resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable result determined under French tax rules and reconcile it to the accounting result through the required schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income attributable to the French SAS. Do not report a foreign shareholder's unrelated income as the SAS's income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, tax computation and payment section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute IS, applicable contributions, instalments, credits, and the balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the rate and relief conditions applicable to the SAS; foreign ownership alone does not qualify the company for a reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the balance sheet, income statement, and relevant accounting detail under the normal regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use French statutory accounts and French tax accounting adjustments for the SAS; identify related-party balances accurately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit to taxable profit and track tax losses and other tax attributes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only losses and tax attributes legally available to the French SAS, supported by prior returns and records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide prescribed information concerning distributions and related tax matters.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose distributions to foreign shareholders and apply withholding procedures separately from the company's IS computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2572-SD and IS instalment payment references
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report or settle corporate income tax balances and instalments through the applicable electronic payment process.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SAS pays French IS through its own French tax account and is responsible for its own payment obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where applicable, report prescribed information on transactions with associated enterprises and transfer-pricing arrangements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess the statutory filing thresholds and report cross-border related-party transactions involving the French SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2258-SD, country-by-country reporting notification or report
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File the applicable notification or country-by-country report where the French constituent entity is within the statutory multinational group reporting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine the ultimate parent, group consolidated revenue threshold, reporting entity, and French filing obligation; the general threshold is EUR 750 million of consolidated group revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases of fraudulent activity or concealed activity, subject to statutory conditions. Late payment generally incurs interest of 0.20% per month and may also attract a 5% collection surcharge. Material inaccuracies may trigger tax reassessments, interest, and penalties generally ranging from 40% to 80%, depending on conduct and proof.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident entity, the domestic withholding rate is generally 25%, subject to treaty relief and statutory exemptions. A qualifying EU parent may obtain an exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, subject to ownership, holding-period, beneficial-owner, anti-abuse, and other conditions. Rates and procedures differ for individual recipients.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the payer with the appropriate French treaty-relief certificate, generally the relevant Form 5000 and, for dividends, Form 5001, duly completed and certified by the recipient's tax authority where required. The payer applies relief at source only when documentation and statutory conditions are satisfied; otherwise, withholding is made at the domestic rate and the recipient may claim a refund using the prescribed forms and supporting evidence. Confirm residence, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions, and any applicable anti-abuse rule under the specific treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a French payer to a non-resident are generally subject to 25% domestic withholding, subject to an applicable treaty reduction or exemption and EU law relief where conditions are met. Interest paid to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding under domestic law, subject to exceptions, including payments to recipients in non-cooperative jurisdictions and anti-abuse rules; the applicable rate and exceptions must be checked for the payment and recipient. Treaty rates are treaty-specific and must not be assumed without reviewing the relevant convention.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer-pricing documentation is generally required where the French entity, or a qualifying related entity in its ownership chain, has annual turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or meets specified ownership or control links to an entity meeting that threshold. A simplified annual transfer-pricing statement is generally required for entities meeting the lower statutory threshold, currently EUR 50 million in turnover or gross assets, subject to the applicable statutory conditions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a general standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. French tax authorities may nevertheless challenge arrangements lacking commercial substance or genuine economic activity under domestic anti-abuse, transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, permanent-establishment, and treaty anti-abuse rules. The SAS should maintain evidence of decision-making, personnel, premises, operational capacity, risk control, and functions consistent with its energy-trading activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax fraud and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing taxable income, fabricating expenses or invoices, submitting knowingly false returns, or organizing fraudulent withholding or VAT claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest, and penalties that may reach 80% of the evaded tax. Criminal tax fraud may be punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated cases may carry higher penalties, including up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability where their own conduct satisfies the offense elements. A court may order publication, confiscation, or other ancillary penalties. Personal recovery of unpaid tax may be ordered in specified cases of fraudulent or repeated non-compliance; imprisonment or travel restrictions are not automatic consequences of an ordinary corporate tax debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to provide required documentation or reporting, mispricing related-party crude oil, fuel, financing, services, or intellectual-property transactions, or lacking evidence that the reported method reflects the arm's-length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, late-payment interest, and applicable accuracy penalties may apply. Failure to provide required full documentation may attract a specific fine based on the greater of EUR 10,000 or the statutory proportion of the reassessed profits or relevant transactions, subject to the applicable legal rules and limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is primarily liable for tax adjustments and administrative penalties. A director may incur personal liability for intentional participation in fraud or other offenses; no automatic veil piercing follows solely from a transfer-pricing adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit distribution or withholding-tax failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without satisfying corporate-law requirements, misrepresenting shareholder residence or beneficial ownership, or failing to withhold and remit tax when required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and penalties. Directors may incur civil or criminal exposure if they knowingly authorize unlawful distributions or participate in fraudulent filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability depends on the director's conduct and the applicable statutory or civil-law basis; it is not automatic for a payment or withholding error.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, sanctions evasion, and illicit commodity trade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly processing proceeds of crime, concealing beneficial ownership or the origin of funds, breaching applicable EU or French sanctions, or structuring crude-oil and marine-fuel transactions to evade restrictions or reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is generally punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with increased penalties for aggravated circumstances. Sanctions breaches may carry substantial criminal and administrative penalties under applicable French and EU law, depending on the conduct and instrument breached.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees may be prosecuted for their own knowing participation. Confiscation and other ancillary penalties may apply. Travel restrictions are not an automatic sanction and require a separate lawful basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting regulated wholesale or intermediary activities without required authorization, failing to comply with applicable energy-market, customs, product-safety, sanctions, or excise obligations, or misdescribing fuel origin or product characteristics.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions depend on the specific activity and breached regime and may include administrative fines, suspension or withdrawal of authorization, tax and customs assessments, seizure, and criminal penalties where an offense is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may be personally liable for an offense in which the director participated or for a specific statutory duty breached. Liability is not established solely by the company's failure; the applicable sectoral rule and facts control.
